findings.title: The new shared-customer guard erases a co-tenant who has not passed the point of no return, and still both-siblings-skips one status over
findings.reason:
The fix replaced ao.status = 'purged' with ao.mode = 'delete_data' AND ao.status IN ('purge_scheduled','purged'). It keys on status; the property it needs is 'this sibling can no longer come back', and the branch's own D5-inversion argument (PurgeWorker.ts:96-99) names purge_started_at as that marker. The sets differ in BOTH directions. W1: keep-my-data.ts:192-199 admits a cancellation when mode='delete_data' AND status IN ('pending','tearing_down','purge_scheduled') AND terminal_at IS NULL AND purge_started_at IS NULL AND purge_cancelled_at IS NULL. Intersecting that with the guard's exclusion set yields status='purge_scheduled' with purge_started_at IS NULL - the ENTIRE purge grace window, the modal state of every delete_data offboarding between teardown and purge_after. So when account A purges while co-tenant B sits anywhere in its own grace window, A's guard excludes B, counts zero live co-tenants and redacts the shared Customer; B can still click Keep my data, whose entire purpose is do not destroy my data, and B's Stripe billing contact has already been destroyed irreversibly by another tenant's purge with nothing recorded against B. The docblock premise 'Both are being deleted, so redacting the shared Customer harms neither' is false for a purge_scheduled sibling: it is SCHEDULED for deletion, not committed to it. W2: markPurgeTerminalFailure leaves status='failed' with purge_started_at set (PurgeWorker.ts:131), and 'failed' is outside the exclusion set, so a sibling unambiguously past the point of no return is counted as a live co-tenant and A skips - the both-siblings-skip class the fix set out to remove, one status over, reachable whenever a sibling's purge exhausts its BullMQ attempts. Both vanish with AND ao.purge_started_at IS NOT NULL AND ao.purge_cancelled_at IS NULL, which still closes the concurrent-purge case because AccountOffboardingPurgePoller.ts:126 stamps purge_started_at in the claim transaction before either job runs. Why it shipped: the predicate has no behavioural test - every stage test mocks sql and pushes {count:0}/{count:1}, the offboarding live-DB suite never exercises it, and the only pin is the byte-for-byte string in scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts:2841, a string comparison that asserts nothing about meaning (inventory U01).

FIXED 2026-09-04 (896312c9..). The predicate is now `ao.purge_started_at IS NOT NULL AND ao.purge_cancelled_at IS NULL`, closing W1 (the purge grace window, where a co-tenant can still cancel) and W2 (a terminally failed sibling, which is past the point of no return). The finding-under-the-finding is closed too: worker/jobs/account-offboarding/__tests__/stripe-customer-redaction-guard.integration.test.ts drives the real stage against real Postgres with real co-tenant rows, 8 cases. Verified as an oracle by reinstating the old status-keyed predicate: 3 of the 8 fail.

findings.title: detachPaymentMethods declares has_more and never reads it; the sibling module in the same directory paginates and throws
findings.reason:
StripePaymentMethodListResult declares has_more: boolean (:105) and nothing reads it. One page of 100 is fetched, the loop detaches what it got, and redactStripeCustomer returns 'redacted'. The justification is a one-line assumption at :253 ('a customer with more attached methods than this is not real'); Stripe caps attached PaymentMethods at no number, and the Billing Portal does not detach the old card when a new one is added. Three things make this more than hypothetical. (1) stripe-invoices.ts - the other Stripe-facing offboarding module, whose isRetryableStripeError this pass's own new docblock calls BYTE-IDENTICAL - declares the same has_more shape (:30), implements bounded cursor pagination (:143-176) and throws a retryable bounded_pagination_exhausted rather than reporting success when the bound is exhausted. (2) The failure is silent and then unrecoverable: 'redacted' lets the purge finalize and runParentTombstonePurgeStage NULLs accounts.stripe_customer_id, leaving no handle to finish - verbatim the outcome stripe-customer-redaction.ts:336-339 gives as the reason not to map permanent errors to success. (3) A retry cannot recover it either: the marker is written on the same run, so isAlreadyRedacted (:228) short-circuits before detachPaymentMethods is reached. Fix: loop on has_more with starting_after as stripe-invoices.ts does, or minimally throw when page.has_more is true. Graded P1 only because the trigger needs >100 attached PaymentMethods on one Customer; the failure class is P0-shaped.

FIXED 2026-09-04 (ecf4c224). detachPaymentMethods now reads has_more, paginates, and throws retryable `bounded_pagination_exhausted` at ten pages rather than returning `redacted` over an unfinished sweep. It re-lists from the START rather than advancing a cursor, because detaching removes the anchor a cursor would point at. Mutation-verified: reinstating the one-page sweep fails 4 tests.

findings.title: Round 1's F04 is not closed - the acked-for-age warning still matches no alert rule, and the new probe has no runbook row either
findings.reason:
docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md is untouched by the entire branch (git diff --name-only b9fb9601..HEAD -- docs/runbooks/ is empty). warnStripeSubscriptionEventAckedForAge emits captureMessage('stripe_subscription_event_acked_for_age') at level warning with tags {feature: 'stripe_subscription_out_of_order', event_type} and NO subsystem tag. Facet comparison against the runbook's rule table: filter - the five live filters are subsystem=health_alert, cost_event=limit_exceeded, feature=stripe_reconciliation, subsystem=import_consent_analytics, feature=solicitation_lane; none matches. Level - runbook section 1 records that a warning captureMessage 'does not reliably classify as high priority' (CONFIG-1), so Sentry's default high-priority rule does not catch it either. Destination - none. That is an emitted operator signal with no rule row, Duty 5's exact definition, and it is the signal D9 leans on: the shared docblock calls it 'the operator's only handle on the acked event'. The pass answered F04 with a DIFFERENT signal - checkStaleIgnoredInboundEvents, which does route via rule 1's subsystem:health_alert and is fine - covering the aggregate stream but not the per-event handle. Second half: the new probe has no section 1 checklist bullet, despite section 1 carrying the explicit precedent 'Rule 6 is a REPLACEMENT, not an addition (#967)', written because an ack took events out of checkFailedInboundEvents' set and a replacement rule was therefore mandatory - the same move this branch makes on the Stripe lane. Fix: add a section 1 bullet plus a frequency-conditioned rule row for feature:stripe_subscription_out_of_order (the capture title is a constant, so a first-seen rule fires once ever), and a section 1 bullet recording the new probe as a replacement.

FIXED 2026-09-04 (3170d108). docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md gains rule 7 (`feature` equals `stripe_subscription_out_of_order`, frequency-conditioned, warning) plus two section-1 checklist bullets — one for the per-event handle, one recording checkStaleIgnoredInboundEvents as a REPLACEMENT on rule 6's precedent. The dead-man switch step renumbers 7 -> 8, per the runbook's own rule that step and rule numbers must not collide.

findings.title: The events arm was split in two and its saturation reporting was not - the warning now miss-fires and the count hides which arm is backed up
findings.reason:
ArchivalPoller.ts:109-112 claims 'each arm saturates and reports independently, and the low-volume arm cannot starve behind the high-volume one'. The first half is false: the query returns ONE combined count (:132) and :472 compares it against a single BATCH_LIMIT = 5000 whose true cap for this arm is now 10000. False positive: processed deletes 3000 (arm exhausted, nothing remains) and stale_ignored deletes 2000 (arm exhausted) gives eventsCount = 5000, so the poller warns 'Batch limit reached - more rows may remain' when neither arm saturated and nothing remains; reachable across the whole [5000, 9999] band. ArchivalPoller.ts:212 already names this class by hand ('saturation warnings could miss-fire'). Lost attribution: the Archived log's events: key (:456) is now the sum of two different retention arms, so an operator cannot see a growing acked-for-age backlog at all. This diverges from an idiom the same file established for the same situation - arms 9 and 10 are one table split into two arms for the same index reason and carry TWO counts and TWO saturation entries, with ArchivalPoller.test.ts:420-422 stating why: 'Two arms, two saturation signals: arm 9 draining while arm 10 is pinned at the cap has to be visible.' Fix: return two counts (GROUP BY status in the deleted CTE, or two statements) and report events_processed / events_stale_ignored separately. No test covers the current semantics (inventory U02).

FIXED 2026-09-04 (ecf4c224). The inbound_events sweep is now TWO statements with two counts and two saturation entries (`events_processed` / `events_stale_ignored`), following arms 9 and 10 in the same file. Closes the [5000, 9999] false positive and the lost attribution. Mutation-verified: summing the two saturation counts fails 2 tests.

findings.title: The factory / lazy-getStripe fix is unpinned - hoisting the resolve above the null check passes its covering test
findings.reason:
Mutation M7: hoist 'const stripe = resolveStripe();' above the 'if (!customerId)' early return, reverting the change to eager resolution. Baseline green, mutant PASSED. Arbiter reasoning is recorded on inventory row M7 and reproduced here: the covering test's named contract is 'is a no-op when the offboarding row carries no stripe_customer_id' and its comment justifies it as 'issuing a Stripe call here would spend a network round trip'; both still hold under the mutant, which issues no Stripe call and no SQL. The mutant breaks a different property, the one purge-stages.ts:764-768 states - 'getStripe() throws when STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is unset, and resolving it eagerly made every delete_data purge depend on the key, including accounts that never had a Stripe Customer at all'. No test asserts that property, so the survivor is on a property this test never asserts and is classified inconclusive/oracle rather than a P0. The PurgeWorker test's expect.any(Function) pins that a function is passed, not that resolution is deferred; the stage tests pass () => fakeStripe(), which never throws. FIXED 2026-09-04 (3170d108). A test passing a factory that throws pins the property the code states — getStripe() throws without STRIPE_SECRET_KEY — which is what mutation M7 actually broke and what the old contract ("no Stripe call and no SQL") could not see. Re-running M7 now fails that test.

findings.title: D6's recorded reason for not delivering the receipt's erasure clause is false - the conditioning mechanism ships in the same payload
findings.reason:
D6 records: 'The promised clause would be FALSE in the skipped_shared_customer outcome, and the template has no outcome data to condition on.' The first half is a sound reason not to ship the clause unconditionally. The second half is false. src/lib/shared/worker-types.ts:386-391 carries retained_suppression_count on the purge_receipt payload, with the docblock 'Snapshotted inside the finalize transaction rather than queried at send time ... a retried send has to render the SAME number, and it keeps the email worker ignorant of the solicitation domain'; src/lib/account-offboarding/outbox.ts:45-50 carries the matching enqueue field. The redaction outcome is written into account_offboardings.provider_dispositions by an earlier transaction of the same job (purge-stages.ts:838, appendStripeCustomerRedactionRecord) and finalizePurgeInTransaction, which enqueues the receipt, runs last - so the outcome is committed and readable at exactly the moment retained_suppression_count is snapshotted, by exactly the same mechanism, for exactly the same reason. This is not a demand to ship the clause; the owner may still prefer a retention-only receipt. The finding is that the durable record gives an infeasibility reason that is not true, so a future session reading D6 will conclude the option was closed when it is one snapshotted field away - the 'confident prose that is in fact the defect' pattern D7 itself names. Fix: amend D6 to state the actual reason, or condition the clause on a snapshotted outcome.

FIXED 2026-09-04 (3170d108). D6's recorded reason is corrected. retained_suppression_count is snapshotted onto the same purge_receipt payload in the same finalize transaction, so the option is one field away rather than infeasible. The DECISION stands and is now recorded on its real grounds — a conditional erasure sentence on a compliance email is a scope and legal-review question this branch did not open.

findings.title: 'A stale_ignored rate probe restores the pager the ack removed' overstates what the probe restores - single-orphan coverage is gone
findings.reason:
Partially true. Before the ack a SINGLE orphaned customer paged continuously for Stripe's roughly 3-day retry schedule, because reclaim resets received_at (worker/ingress/shared.ts:62-70) and checkFailedInboundEvents' threshold is 0 (checks.ts:302-303). After the ack that row leaves the failed set, and the new probe's threshold is 5 per hour per (source, event_type), so the single-orphan case now pages nothing; only a stream is restored. checks.ts:52-58 is honest about the threshold and why it is 5 - the two durable records above are the ones that overstate. Small, but it is the sentence a future operator will read when one customer silently fails to provision.

FIXED 2026-09-04 (3170d108). Both overstating records corrected — deviation D6 and the tenant-scope allowlist note now say the probe restores the AGGREGATE stream only, that the single-orphan case pages nothing through it (threshold 5/hour vs the failed probe's 0), and that the per-event handle is rule 7, a separate signal. The runbook states the same limit so an operator is not surprised by it.

findings.title: The new probe's window column and threshold boundary are unasserted, and the window column silently diverges from its sibling probe
findings.reason:
checks.test.ts asserts status = 'stale_ignored' and GROUP BY source, event_type in the query text and exercises counts 40 (fires) and 3 (quiet). Neither the window column nor the boundary is pinned. Substituting received_at for processed_at passes both tests - the choice is correct (markInboundEventStaleIgnored stamps processed_at, worker/ingress/shared.ts:96-101) but unpinned, and it diverges from the sibling probe next door which windows on received_at (checks.ts:300) with no comment explaining why the two differ. count > threshold changed to count >= threshold also passes both tests, silently moving the effective threshold from 6 to 5. Not executed as mutations: the budget was better spent on the six claims the round was convened for, and neither gap changes behaviour at HEAD.

FIXED 2026-09-04 (3170d108). Both substitutions are now pinned, with the reason processed_at is right (the ack stamps it; reclaim resets received_at) so the two sibling probes' different spellings read as deliberate. Mutation-verified: swapping to received_at and flipping > to >= each fail their test.
